title: Converge Learn-it Atlas on one learning journey
purpose: Complete the evidence-backed R5 successor correction explicitly authorized after Human Replay R4: preserve the single existing Atlas learning journey while reducing per-course action competition and translating existing Atlas evidence/recommendations into learner-facing state and next-step semantics. Preserve persisted history, resume, review-needed, lineage, revisions, imports, storage and accessibility behavior.
invariants: Atlas learning actions from Today and Library enter the same existing Atlas planner/session engine; no third runtime or learner mode is introduced.
An active Atlas activity hides Today chrome, the classic Library surface, unrelated Atlas course rows and replanning controls while keeping prompt and answers contiguous.

R5 changes only action hierarchy and learner-facing projections: each Atlas course exposes one dominant learning action, 5/15/30 remains available through one compact duration selector when a new plan is needed, and resume remains a single direct action when a resumable session exists.

Learner-facing course state and next-step copy are derived only from the existing Atlas objective evidence and existing recommendation ranking; no new scoring, planning or persistence algorithm is introduced.

Detailed objective evidence remains available on demand; the default summary emphasizes objective state, what needs reinforcement when applicable, and the next learner action before historical counts/dates.
The final activity remains visible with its own feedback and an explicit Voir le bilan action before the summary is rendered.
Atlas event commits, history, resume state, review-needed semantics, package/course/activity lineage, revision IDs/digests and import behavior are unchanged.
No storage schema, database version, migration, backend, account or sync behavior is introduced.
learnit.kit.v2 and all EPF kit payloads remain unchanged.
Keyboard/focus behavior remains based on the existing Atlas controls and focus assertions, with native select/button semantics and minimum target sizing preserved.
requiredEvidence: PR scope validates exactly against ATLAS-WP-024.
Learn-it Next CI runs the bounded atlas-ux-convergence profile inside the existing workflow on the exact PR head, using only the current build and existing relevant tests.

Existing Atlas integration and UX clarity tests cover Library routing, exclusive active surface, one-primary-action course hierarchy, compact duration selection, Atlas-derived learner state/next step, final feedback before Voir le bilan, action-oriented summary disclosure and compacted learner-facing import presentation.
The deterministic Learn-it Next source manifest is rebound to every changed manifest-owned source.
Before/after evidence is prepared for Today action count, Library action count, learner-facing course state/next step, summary meaning, final feedback-to-bilan separation and import density.
No learner usability PASS is declared before the R5 human replay.
adversarialTests: apps/learnit-next/tests/atlas_m1_int.py checks that Atlas Library actions cannot fall through to the classic learning handler, active sessions suppress competing surfaces, R5 action hierarchy remains bound to the existing Atlas entrypoint, and learner-facing progress semantics do not alter runtime ownership.

apps/learnit-next/tests/atlas_m2_ux_clarity.py checks one-primary-action course presentation, compact duration selection, objective-labelled next-step summary semantics and the final-feedback-to-bilan transition while retaining prior Atlas UX clarity coverage.
nonGoals: Changing EPF kits or the learnit.kit.v2 contract.
Migrating or merging classic and Atlas storage.
Adding backend, accounts, sync, a theory/discovery mode, a third runtime or a broad dashboard redesign.
Adding search, filtering, sorting, shelves/collections, new navigation architecture or unrelated visual polish.
Changing Atlas recommendation ranking, planner policy, evidence state transitions or learning-event semantics.
Creating a new contradictory-QA chain or declaring human usability PASS.
independentReview: Issue #352 remains the implementation authority; the user explicitly authorized GO_R5_BOUNDED_ACTION_HIERARCHY_LEARNER_PROGRESS_SEMANTICS after the completed Human Replay R4.

Human Replay R4 on exact candidate 271a4f2dd9e4403771607c2d84c037fa2e7bd2f3 is the evidence basis: course-list topology improved, while action competition and learner comprehension of progress/summary remained material frictions.
A short R5 human replay owns the learner-usability verdict; this implementation stream must not self-certify UX PASS.
rollback: Close or revert PR #354. The baseline storage, contracts, EPF kits and pre-existing Atlas/classic persisted data remain unchanged.
